notes:
I found sources for every verse, but they cover the chapter unevenly. My searches didn't turn up anything from the Catholic, Orthodox or modern-scholarship sites, and nothing on hyper-grace or word of faith, so those parts are missing. There's a list of gaps at the end.

---

**v. 1**
- Guzik: Paul's word for "foolish" means someone who *can* think but doesn't use that ability. They had the knowledge but weren't using it. "Bewitched" isn't meant literally. Their thinking was so clouded it was as if a spell had been cast on them. "Clearly portrayed" is like putting something up on a billboard. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/
- Spurgeon (quoted by Precept Austin): Jesus Christ had been so clearly set forth before them that they might, as it were, see Him as He hung upon the cross of Calvary. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians-3-commentary

**v. 2**
- Guzik: The Holy Spirit is a gift received by simple faith, not a prize earned by works of the law. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/
- Maxie Dunnam (Methodist; quoted by Precept Austin): The "hearing of faith" is a hearing that is open to the gospel and leads the hearer to trust Christ. Hearing the gospel creates faith (God gives us that faith) in which the Spirit is received. https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/61890/

**v. 3**
- Guzik: The Galatians were deceived into thinking that spiritual growth or maturity could be achieved through the works of the flesh, instead of a continued simple faith and abiding in Jesus. His summary: under law we grow by "earning and deserving," under grace by "believing and receiving." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/

**v. 4**
- Guzik gives two readings:
  - The Galatians may have suffered persecution, and Acts 14 records persecution in Galatia.
  - The phrase may be better translated as having had wonderful *spiritual experiences* for nothing. Guzik thinks this fits the context better.
  
  https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/

**v. 5**
- Guzik: God supplied the Holy Spirit in response to faith. Miracles are wrought by faith. He applies this to believers who feel they lack blessing: the cause is not that they haven't earned enough, but that they aren't putting their faith in Jesus. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/
- Pentecostal (Assemblies of God): According to Galatians 3:1–5 and 13–14, a believer can claim new life in the Spirit by faith. but one cannot claim material prosperity with the same confidence. https://enrichmentjournal.ag.org/Issues/2015/Winter-2015/The-Prosperity-Gospel-A-Biblical-Evaluation

**v. 6**
- Guzik: Righteousness was credited to Abraham before he was circumcised. Guzik counts Genesis 15:6 among the clearest texts in the Bible on salvation by grace through faith alone.
  - He cites Calvin: Abraham trusted the promised Mediator.
  - He cites Poole: Abraham's faith was not itself his righteousness.
  - He notes that the ancient rabbis tended to praise Abraham for keeping the law rather than for his faith, so Paul's use of Abraham would have surprised his opponents.
  
  https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/

**v. 7**
- Guzik: What links people to Abraham is faith, not genetics or works. This rebuked Jewish believers who felt superior, and comforted Gentiles who were treated as second-class.
- **A real disagreement:** Guzik warns that this verse has been misused to support "replacement theology," the idea that the Church inherits all of Israel's promises. He says Abraham has both spiritual and genetic sons, and God has a plan for both. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/
- Spurgeon (quoted by Precept Austin): Race no longer matters here. Believers are a new race born by God's will. https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/61890/

**vv. 8–9**
- Guzik: The point is to destroy the idea that a Gentile must first become a Jew in order to become a Christian. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/
- Matthew Henry: Scripture "foresees" because its Author foresaw it. Gentiles are blessed in the same way Abraham was, by being justified. William Kelly: the law offers blessing but never gives it. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/galatians/3-14.html

**v. 10**
- Guzik: To stand approved under the law you must do *all* of it. If you don't, you are cursed. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/
- Spurgeon: Since no one has kept everything in the law, everyone under the law has incurred the curse. https://www.preceptaustin.org/spurgeon_on_galatians_3

**v. 11**
- Barber: Paul goes from Deuteronomy to Habakkuk to show that the way we live after salvation is also by faith, not only salvation itself. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians_3_commentary-barber
- Gutzke: "The just shall live by faith" means living by believing God's promises. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians-3-commentary

**v. 12**
- Guzik: Paul quotes Leviticus 18:5 against the idea of "I'll do my best and faith covers the rest." Paul shows from the Old Testament that this isn't good enough. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians-3-commentary

**v. 13**
- Guzik: "Redeemed" means to buy back. The price was Jesus himself. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/
- Spurgeon: Salvation rests in Christ, the representative Man who alone delivers us from the law's curse. https://www.preceptaustin.org/spurgeon_on_galatians_3
- Bible Hub notes: The curse we deserved fell on Jesus and satisfied God's justice. https://biblehub.com/galatians/3-14.htm

**v. 14**
- What "the blessing of Abraham" means:
  - Clarke: justification, or pardon of sin, with the blessings that follow it.
  - Barnes and Gill: chiefly justification.
  - Calvin: if Jews must be freed from the law to be Abraham's heirs, nothing stops Gentiles from receiving the same benefit.
  - Constable: two blessings, justification and the Spirit's ministry.
  
  https://www.studylight.org/commentary/galatians/3-14.html
- Guzik: Jesus took the curse we deserved so we could receive the blessing he deserved. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/
- **Debated popular teaching (prosperity gospel):** The Assemblies of God describes the prosperity view this way: by removing the law's curse, the cross opens the door to the law's blessings, which include prosperity. Its own answer is that in this passage the blessing is justification by faith and the gift of new life in the Spirit. https://enrichmentjournal.ag.org/Issues/2015/Winter-2015/The-Prosperity-Gospel-A-Biblical-Evaluation

**vv. 15–16**
- My sources say little about v. 15. Bible Hub's study note says the promised offspring is fulfilled ultimately in Christ. https://biblehub.com/galatians/3-14.htm
- Coffman: Gentiles become part of Christ's spiritual body and so belong to the singular "seed," which is Christ. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/galatians/3-14.html

**v. 17**
- Wuest: The 430-year gap shows that the law was something new and different, not part of the promise. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians-3-commentary
- Barber: The covenant with Abraham rested on promise, not on his works. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians_3_commentary-barber

**v. 18**
- Guzik: An inheritance based on law would depend partly on Abraham's obedience and so might not be permanent. One based on promise stands sure. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/

**v. 19**
- Guzik: The law was added to hold back sin by revealing God's standard, and also to stir up our rebellion so we see our need of Christ. The law isn't revoked, but it is no longer the ground on which we approach God. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/ and https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians-3-commentary
- Spurgeon: Under the Holy Spirit's hand, the law makes us see how evil sin is. https://www.preceptaustin.org/spurgeon_on_galatians_3
- Griffith-Thomas: The law was a sort of parenthesis, not God's original or final purpose. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians-3-commentary

**v. 20**
- MacArthur: The Greek is hard. Paul seems to mean that a mediator is needed only when there are two parties. God gave the covenant directly to Abraham, who was a witness and beneficiary, not a party to it. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians-3-commentary
- Boice (quoted by Guzik): The law was two-sided. The promise is one-sided. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/

**v. 21**
- Guzik: The law isn't evil. Its problem is that it can't give strength to those who want to keep it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/

**v. 22**
- Guzik: Sin is the prison bars, Scripture put us in the cell, and only faith opens the door. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/
- Boice: This verse sums up Romans 1–3. Morris: the law turns out to be a jailer, and faith is the only way out. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians-3-commentary

**v. 23**
- Stott: The law's oppressive work was temporary and meant ultimately to bless, shutting us up until Christ should set us free. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians-3-commentary

**v. 24**
- Lutheran (Luther): The law is in charge only until it has led us to Christ. It doesn't justify hypocrites, but it drives the contrite to Christ. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians-3-commentary
- Guzik: The law protects by showing God's heart and the best way to live, and by giving a foundation for civil law. If the law isn't presented in a way that leads people to Jesus, it isn't presented properly. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/

**v. 25**
- Guzik: Once faith has come, we are no longer under the tutor. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/

**v. 26**
- W. F. Adeney (Pulpit Commentary homiletics): This sonship isn't natural to everyone. It comes by adoption, through faith and union with Christ. https://biblehub.com/sermons/galatians/3-27.htm

**v. 27: a real Protestant disagreement over baptism**
- **Lutheran (Luther):** Putting on Christ is a new birth done in baptism (Titus 3:5). Those baptized are regenerate. He rebukes those who belittle baptism. https://biblehub.com/sermons/galatians/3-27.htm
- **Bishop Moberly:** In baptism we were planted into Christ's body, the Church, and the Spirit's life was begun in us. That life must then grow. https://biblehub.com/sermons/galatians/3-27.htm
- **F. W. Robertson:** He mocks the idea that the Spirit must wait on the exact timing of the ceremony. https://biblehub.com/sermons/galatians/3-27.htm
- **Gill (Baptist):** Baptism doesn't bring a person into *union* with Christ, but into communion with him. Immersion is "a lively emblem" of his death and resurrection. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/galatians/3-27.html
- **Matthew Henry:** In baptism they professed their faith and, as it were, put on Christ's livery. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/wnt/galatians/3-27.html
- **Wuest and Got Questions:** This is Spirit baptism into union with Christ, not water baptism. Got Questions rejects baptismal regeneration here. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians-3-commentary and https://www.gotquestions.org/baptism-Galatians-3-27.html
- **Wuest on "clothed":** The word isn't about wearing a mask. It means entering a real relationship with someone. **Barclay:** possibly an allusion to the white robes worn at baptism, a custom attested only later. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians-3-commentary and https://www.studylight.org/commentary/galatians/3-27.html

**v. 28: a real disagreement over men's and women's roles**
- Traditional reading:
  - Ellicott: The verse swept away the ancient world's artificial distinctions.
  - Barnes: The verse doesn't abolish the distinction between the sexes. Neither sex has any special advantage for salvation.
  
  https://biblehub.com/commentaries/galatians/3-28.htm
- The Gospel Coalition (complementarian): It acknowledges that egalitarians treat this verse as a central text, but it insists that equality doesn't rule out differences in design. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/essay/the-roles-of-men-and-women/
- Got Questions: The context is salvation, not church roles. https://www.gotquestions.org/neither-male-nor-female.html
- Bible.org survey of views:
  - Schreiner and Johnson: equality in salvation, not a statement about how the church functions.
  - The Winstons: sex differences are no longer taken into account.
  - Lee-Barnewall: Paul's stress is relational unity.
  
  https://blogs.bible.org/male-and-female-one-in-christ-galatians-328-what-it-means-for-women-beyond-salvation/
- Guzik: Every dividing line is erased for standing before God. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-3/

**v. 29**
- Wuest: The Judaizers taught that keeping the law made Gentiles Abraham's seed. Paul says this comes by faith in Christ. The issue was life (salvation), not land. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians-3-commentary
- Adeney: Christians enjoy the fulfilment of promises that the Jew held as a hope. https://biblehub.com/sermons/galatians/3-27.htm

---

**Gaps.** I didn't find anything from:
- the Catholic and Orthodox sites (newadvent, catholic.com, oca.org);
- the modern-scholarship sites (bibleodyssey.org, NET Bible notes). That leaves out the "New Perspective" reading of "works of the law" and the "faith in" versus "faithfulness of" Christ debate on v. 22;
- Reformed sources on the verses where traditions differ;
- any discussion of hyper-grace or word-of-faith teaching on this chapter.

I also couldn't read most of the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary notes verse by verse, and coverage of vv. 15–16 and 26 is thin. Those are the places to research next.
